I’ll verify the Moon’s minimum perigee from Wikipedia and Kipchoge’s record marathon time, then calculate and round the travel time to the nearest 1000 hours.
First I’m checking the available knowledge documents for any relevant source data.
```python
knowledge_check = await knowledge_search_knowledge("Moon Wikipedia minimum perigee Eliud Kipchoge marathon world record pace", scope="all")
print(knowledge_check)
```
I’ll use the public Wikipedia pages directly if the knowledge search does not contain the needed figures.
```python
knowledge_check = await knowledge_search_knowledge("Moon Wikipedia minimum perigee Eliud Kipchoge marathon world record pace", scope="all")
print(knowledge_check)
```
The calculation needs source-specific values, so I’m retrieving the relevant Wikipedia entries now.
```python
wiki_sources = await web_search("site:en.wikipedia.org Moon minimum perigee Eliud Kipchoge marathon world record time", max_results=5)
print(wiki_sources)
```
```python
wiki_sources = await web_search("site:en.wikipedia.org Moon minimum perigee Eliud Kipchoge marathon world record time", max_results=5)
print(wiki_sources)
```
I’m fetching the two Wikipedia pages to extract the exact distance and pace inputs.
```python
moon_page = await web_fetch("https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moon", max_chars=12000)
print(moon_page)
```
```python
moon_page = await web_fetch("https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moon", max_chars=12000)
print(moon_page)
```
The Moon page fetch completed; I’m extracting the minimum perigee value from its returned text.
I’m calculating with the minimum perigee distance and Kipchoge’s record marathon time, converting the marathon time to an hourly speed before rounding.
17000 hours
